decisions.reason: As a recently launched cardboard display with its own webpage and clear fit to the firm's core display business, management is likely to keep backing it and attribute any early weakness to normal market ramp-up.

The firm has visibly committed to this cardboard display variant and, given its close relation to established paper-based merchandising products, escalation of commitment makes withdrawal unlikely after only one year.
This quarter-pallet cardboard display sits squarely in the company's core competence and public product offering, so management would be inclined to continue rather than reverse course quickly.
Although this eighth-pallet format may be somewhat more specialized, it is still a core cardboard display product and the firm is likely to persist with it while expecting adoption to improve.

This wooden display pallet is less central to a paper-products manufacturer than the cardboard lines, but the recent launch and visible commitment still make management more likely to continue than to withdraw immediately.

Even if the media-products application is narrower, it remains a related quarter-pallet display offering, so management would probably keep it on the market for longer before admitting the launch was unsuccessful.
